# Results — Study 775 (Halloween-Candy)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Hershey (HSY) enjoys a Halloween seasonal run-up**: rallies into Oct 31 because Halloween
is the confectioner's biggest selling season, and (folklore's second half) fades after.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint
`22c38ea72789` (HSY + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `HSY` (Hershey) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 8,411 rows, 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 32 Halloweens 1994→2025, one per year on **October 31** (a fixed public holiday — nothing to "verify" beyond the date). Anchor = last trading close on/before Oct 31 |
| Events resolvable | all **32** of 32 Halloweens have HSY+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (HSY − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: Halloween is Oct 31 every year. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; fade = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** HSY is a consumer-staple with a market beta well below 1, so a raw
`HSY − SPY` difference over a drifting window is partly mechanical. The run-up/fade windows
here are short (2–4 weeks), so beta is a minor contaminant — but it is the reason we quote
the *abnormal* return throughout, never the raw HSY move.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE Halloween (HSY − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 32 | −1.192% | −1.339 | 14/32 = 43.8% [28.2%, 60.7%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 32 | **−2.012%** | **−1.759** | 12/32 = 37.5% [22.9%, 54.7%] |

The bullish folklore is **absent — and, if anything, inverted**: in the run-up *into*
Halloween HSY has, on average, *under*-performed SPY (−1.19% over two weeks, −2.01% over a
month). There is no "rally into the candy season." The 1-month tilt is the strongest cut at
*t* = −1.76 — a whiff of October weakness in the opposite direction of the claim — but it
**does not clear the significance bar** (|*t*| < 2), and the hit rate sits below a coin flip.

## The fade — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER Halloween

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade (k=10) | 32 | −1.080% | −1.319 | 9/32 = 28.1% [15.6%, 45.4%] |
| 1-month fade (k=21) | 32 | −1.119% | −0.919 | 10/32 = 31.2% [18.0%, 48.6%] |

Post-Halloween HSY *also* drifts mildly negative vs SPY, but neither cut is significant
(|*t*| < 1.4). There is no clean "sell the season" reversal to trade either — just a broad,
sub-threshold October-into-November softness relative to the market.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −1.192% | +0.037% (0.830%) | 0.9305 |
| 2-week fade | left | −1.080% | +0.037% (0.830%) | 0.0872 |

The 2-week run-up sits left-of-centre in the luck cloud (right-tail p = 0.93 ⇒ only ~7% of
random 2-week windows were this negative) — a mild anomaly, not a tail event. The fade's
left-tail p = 0.087 is borderline but still north of 0.05. Neither survives as significant.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 1-month run-up *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−1.759**; across all 32 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−2.242, −1.458]** — the negative tilt is **not** driven by a single year (e.g. one crash
into a Halloween); it is a broad, if sub-significant, softness. But its range straddles the
|*t*| = 2 line only at its most extreme leave-one-out, confirming it is borderline at best.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −1.192% (*t* −1.34) | −1.292% (*t* −1.45) | −1.392% (*t* −1.56) |
| 1-month run-up | −2.012% (*t* −1.76) | −2.112% (*t* −1.85) | −2.212% (*t* −1.93) |

The only mildly-interesting version is a *short* of the run-up window (you're shorting a
negative drift), but it never reaches significance gross, let alone net, and shorting a
consumer-staple for a few weeks a year, 32 times, is a capacity-trivial curiosity, not a
strategy. The claimed *long* into Halloween loses money.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.06 (sd 1.20); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  a well-behaved small-sample false-positive rate at n = 32 events with a 10-day AR.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 781):** mean AR +1.08%, *t* = **+1.26**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 781):** mean AR +2.08%, *t* = **+2.41** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically, so the detector would have caught a genuine seasonal run-up had
  one existed.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | The claimed bullish "rally into Halloween" simply is **not there**: every run-up and fade window is *negative* (HSY mildly lags SPY into and out of Oct 31), and **no cut clears |*t*| ≥ 2** (strongest is the 1-month run-up at *t* = −1.76, placebo right-tail 0.93, jackknife [−2.24, −1.46]). The synthetic control shows the detector *would* fire on a real +2% bump (*t* = +2.4), so the absence is informative, not a power failure. Sub-threshold October softness, opposite the folklore — indistinguishable from noise at the desk's bar. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The long-into-Halloween trade *loses* money; the only negative-drift "short" version never reaches significance gross or net, is capacity-trivial (a staple, a few weeks a year), and sits inside a 4-window multiple-testing search. |

**In one sentence:** the "buy Hershey into the Halloween candy season" trade is folklore —
HSY does not rally into Oct 31 (it mildly lags the market both into and out of Halloween),
and no window clears the significance bar, so there is no seasonal run-up to bank.
